argument_summary: The admissible record does not support treating the stale prior approval or the informal monitoring comment as substitutes for current-release documentation. It does support a narrower conclusion: certification is supportable on a caveated basis because aggregate readiness is above threshold, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the governing materials permit launch when current evaluation results and material limitations are documented. The pharmacy prior-authorization regression is the controlling limitation. The correct audit treatment is therefore not full clean compliance and not escalation on the theory that prior approval cures the gap; it is caveated compliance tied to explicit current-release disclosure of the pharmacy subgroup weakness in the release record/model card.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The admissible basis for minimizing escalation is that the evidence supports a bounded caveat path rather than a broader finding that certification is unsupported in all forms.
claims_about_policy: Policy requires that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material weaknesses for named launch use cases be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible evidence already establishes the relevant weakness, establishes that prior approval is stale, and establishes that the monitoring comment is not approved mitigation. On that record, the strongest supportable policy position is that certification may proceed only as caveated compliance contingent on the current release record expressly documenting the pharmacy limitation, not as unconditional compliance and not on the basis of stale approval.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show an approved risk-acceptance artifact.
The current admissible record does not show that the updated model card or release record is already completed.
The pharmacy prior-authorization slice is below threshold for a named launch use case and is a material limitation under the stated policy.
Prior approval from three months ago and the informal monitoring comment are contextual only and cannot by themselves satisfy current-release requirements.
